edges.description: EWS-ATF1 directly occupies the MITF promoter and induces MITF expression, mimicking melanocyte-stimulating hormone (MSH) signaling.
MITF activation is required downstream of EWS-ATF1 for clear cell sarcoma tumor cell survival and proliferation, driving deep soft tissue tumor growth.
Invasion of regional lymphatics leads to frequent sentinel and regional lymph node metastasis.

edges.source: Targeted Receptor Tyrosine Kinase Inhibitor Therapy (Investigational)

nodes.description: The t(12;22)(q13;q12) translocation fuses the EWSR1 gene on chromosome 22 with ATF1 on chromosome 12 in approximately 90% of cases. The fusion protein functions as an aberrant transcription factor that constitutively activates MITF (microphthalmia-associated transcription factor), driving melanocytic differentiation and survival programs.

biological_processes: positive regulation of transcription by RNA polymerase II

nodes.description: Regional lymph node metastasis occurs more commonly than in other soft tissue sarcomas, reflecting the melanocytic biology. Sentinel lymph node biopsy is often performed.

nodes.description: Clear cell sarcoma displays a high propensity for regional lymphatic invasion and sentinel or regional lymph node metastasis, necessitating sentinel lymph node staging and contributing to locoregional recurrence risk.

evidence.snippet: Clinically, CCS commonly involves tendons and aponeuroses, with metastatic potential leading to poor prognoses despite optimal local disease management.

nodes.description: CCS shows MITF expression consistent with activation downstream of the EWSR1-ATF1 fusion. MITF is the master transcription factor of melanocyte lineage and activates genes involved in melanogenesis, cell survival, and proliferation. This explains the melanocytic phenotype despite soft tissue origin.

evidence.reference_title: Clear cell sarcoma shows immunoreactivity for microphthalmia transcription factor: further evidence for melanocytic differentiation.
evidence.snippet: D5 immunoreactivity in clear cell sarcoma provides further evidence for melanocytic differentiation in this unusual tumor.

nodes.description: Downstream of MITF activation, CCS cells express melanocytic markers including S100, HMB45, Melan-A, and tyrosinase. Melanin pigment may be present. However, unlike melanoma, CCS lacks UV-induced mutations and BRAF/NRAS alterations typical of cutaneous melanoma.

evidence.reference_title: Clear cell sarcoma shows immunoreactivity for microphthalmia transcription factor: further evidence for melanocytic differentiation.
evidence.snippet: S-100 protein expression was seen in all 12 cases that had clear cell sarcoma examined. HMB-45 staining was seen in 11 of 12 (92%) tumors. Focal Melan-A positivity was seen in 3 of 7 (43%) tumors.

nodes.description: A slowly growing deep soft tissue mass, most commonly in the foot, ankle, or knee region. The mass is often attached to tendons or aponeuroses. May be present for years before diagnosis.

evidence.reference_title: Clear Cell Sarcoma (CCS) of the Soft Tissue: An Update Narrative Review with Emphasis on the Utility of PRAME in Differential Diagnosis.
evidence.snippet: Clear Cell Sarcoma (CCS) of soft tissue is a rare and highly malignant neoplasm primarily affecting young adults, often presenting in the deep soft tissues of the extremities.

nodes.description: Targeted small-molecule receptor tyrosine kinase inhibitors directed at MET and related angiogenic/RTK pathways (such as crizotinib, pazopanib, sunitinib, and the selective MET inhibitor AMG 337) have been evaluated clinically in advanced or metastatic CCS, though retrospective clinical series show minimal efficacy with immediate progression on sunitinib and pazopanib and only transient disease stabilization in a small subset of patients treated with crizotinib.

nodes.description: Vorinostat is a histone deacetylase (HDAC) inhibitor identified by high-throughput preclinical drug screening in clear cell sarcoma cell lines, where it alters chromatin accessibility and reduces expression of the EWSR1::ATF1 fusion oncogene to suppress tumor cell proliferation.

evidence.reference_title: Targeting the Clear Cell Sarcoma Oncogenic Driver Fusion Gene EWSR1::ATF1 by HDAC Inhibition
evidence.snippet: In this study, we performed a high-throughput drug screening, finding that the histone deacetylase inhibitor vorinostat exerted an antiproliferation effect with the reduced expression of EWSR1::ATF1.
